name: Gerasa water-powered stone saw
summary: At Gerasa (Jerash) a workshop's water channels, wear marks and cut stone suggest a waterwheel drove two sets of multiple saw blades to cut stone before 749 CE.
description: An excavated Gerasa workshop arrangement interpreted as a waterwheel driving two sets of multiple stone-cutting blades, based on water channels, wear and cut stone.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.

date.label: by 749 CE, archaeological horizon
date.basis: The archaeological interpretation places construction after the fifth-century abandonment of the temple and before the 749 earthquake.

events.statement: Multiple parallel cuts and a water-race installation indicate local productive stone sawing in the dated historical horizon.
events.caveats: The mechanism and precise operating dates are reconstructed, and the 749 date is a broad upper limit rather than the start of use.

evidence.locator: pp.149–151, Gerasa archaeological remains and reconstruction
evidence.supports: Wheel race, bearings, circular wear marks and two limestone drums with multiple parallel saw cuts; use before the 749 earthquake is inferred.
